Applicant :- Roshan Ali Qureshi
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

Counsel for Applicant :- Sadrul Islam Jafri,Ambreen Masroor,Sr. Advocate
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Rajeev Misra,J.
1.

Heard Mr. N.I. Jafri, the learned Senior Counsel assisted by Mr. Ambreen Masroor, the learned
counsel for applicant and Mr. Manish Goyal, the learned Additional Advocate General assisted by
Mr. Jai Narayan, the learned A.G.A.-I and Mr. Abhijit Mukharjee, the learned brief holder for State.
2. Perused the record.

3.  This is a repeat application for anticipatory bail filed by applicant-Roshan Ali Qureshi in connection with Case Crime No. 498 of 2019, under Sections 420, 447, 467, 468, 471 IPC, Police Station-Kotwali, District-Rampur during the pendency of trial.

4. Applicant earlier approached this Court by means of Criminal Misc. Anticipatory Bail Application Roshan Ali Qureshi vs State Of U.P. on 19 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93103372/
1 No. 87 of 2020 (Roshan Ali Qureshi Vs. State of U.P. and Another).

sentences.text: In the aforesaid application, an interim order dated 06.01.2020 was passed by this Court.
For ready reference, the same is re-
produced hereinunder:-

"Heard learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Amit Kumar, the learned Brief Holder for the State and perused the record.
The instant bail application has been moved seeking anticipatory bail in light of the apprehension of the arrest of the applicant in Case Crime No. 498 of 2019, under Sections 420, 447, 467, 468, 471 I.P.C., Police Station Kotwali, District- Rampur.
For the purposes of evaluating the prayer for anticipatory bail, the Court notes that the F.I.R. allegations do not establish the requirement of custodial interrogation of the applicant, who is the Registrar of the university concerned.
Additionally, it is relevant to note that the alleged incident is of 2015 whereas the F.I.R. in that respect came to be lodged only in 2019.
Bearing in mind the threat and apprehension as expressed, let learned A.G.A. file a reply/obtain instructions within a period of three weeks.
List on the expiry of the aforesaid period.

Roshan Ali Qureshi vs State Of U.P. on 19 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93103372/

sentences.text: In case of default or breach of any of the aforementioned conditions it shall be open to the Investigating Officer to file an appropriate application before this Court for cancellation of the interim anticipatory bail granted.

Order Date :- 6.1.2020"
5.
Unfortunately, aforementioned application for anticipatory bail came to be dismissed for want of prosecution vide order dated 14.09.2022.

The same reads as under:-
"List has been revised.
Neither the counsel for the applicant nor the counsel for the informant is present.
Learned A.G.A. for the State is present.
As such, with the efflux of time, the anticipatory bail application seems to have become infructuous.
The same is dismissed for want of prosecution and being infructuous.
Interim order, if any, stands vacated.
In the interregnum, the charge sheet was submitted against applicant.
Accordingly, applicant has been charge sheeted under Sections 420 and 120B IPC.

7. Learned counsel for applicant contends that no offence under Section 420 IPC is made out against applicant inasmuch as from the papers accompanying the police report, it cannot be inferred that there was an intention on the part of applicant to cheat right from the inception.
He secondly submits that an offence under Section 120B IPC is subject to trial evidence as conspiracy is a closed door affair.
On the above premise and also on the fact that applicant is an old man aged about 83 years, the liberty of applicant is liable to be protected by this Court.
He has also derived sustenance from the provisions contained in proviso to Section 437 Cr.P.C.

On the cumulative strength of above,
he submits that liberty of applicant is liable to be protected by this Court, by extending the benefit of anticipatory bail.
8. Per contra, the learned Additional Advocate Genral has vehementaly opposed the present application for anticipatory bail.
He submits that initially bailable warrant was issued against applicant on 06.10.2020 which remained in operation up to 08.05.2023.

However, irrespective of above, applicant failed to honour the warrant issued by court below was thus constrained to issue non-bailable warrant against applicant vide order dated 08.05.2023.
9.

At this juncture, the learned Additional Advocate General invited the attention of Court to the judgment of Supreme Court in State of M.P. Vs. Pradeep Sharma (2014) 2 SCC 171 and on basis Roshan Ali Qureshi vs State Of U.P. on 19 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93103372/
3

entities.text: State of M.P. Vs. Pradeep Sharma (2014) 2 SCC 171
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Roshan Ali Qureshi vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: thereof, it is urged that since coercive process has been issued against applicant, therefore, applicant is not entitled to the discretion of this Court under Section 438 Cr.P.C.
As such, present anticipatory bail application is liable to be rejected.

10. Having heard, the learned Senior Counsel for applicant, the learned Additional Advocate General for State and upon perusal of record, this Court finds that it is an undisputed fact that coercive process has been issued against applicant.
Consequently, ratio laid down by Supreme Court in the case of Pradeep Sharma (Supra) is clearly attracted in the present case.
Moreover, the facts disclosed by the Additional Advocate General also cannot be ignored.
11. Resultantly, the prayer for anticipatory bail is refused.
12. However, court below is directed to decide the application for bail of applicant expeditiously.
13. With the aforesaid directions, this application for anticipatory bail stands finally disposed off.
